items.correct_rationale: Option C is correct: the practice rule requires mirrors first, a signal held for at least two seconds, an over-shoulder blind-spot look, then a safe merge before cancelling.

options.rationale: Wrong: mirrors alone leave the blind spot unchecked, so this option omits a required step.
options.text: Check mirrors only then move over

options.rationale: Wrong: signalling after moving gives no advance warning and skips the blind-spot check.
options.text: Merge first then signal briefly

options.rationale: The practice rule requires mirrors, a sustained signal, a blind-spot check, and a safe merge.
options.text: Check mirrors, signal for at least two seconds, check blind spot, then merge safely

options.rationale: Wrong: cancelling before merging removes the warning while the move is still happening.
options.text: Signal then cancel before starting to merge

items.stem: Practice question: you plan a lane change on a multi-lane road. Which sequence matches the taught practice rule?

items.correct_rationale: Option B is correct: the practice rule keeps the car inside marked lanes, finishes a turn in the lane matching the entry lane, and avoids lane changes inside intersections.

options.rationale: Wrong: changing lanes inside the intersection breaks the taught lane-discipline rule.
options.text: Change lanes while crossing the intersection to reach the faster lane

options.rationale: Staying laned and finishing in the corresponding lane reflects the taught rule.
options.text: Stay in marked lanes and finish the turn in the lane you started from

options.rationale: Wrong: finishing in any open lane ignores the corresponding-lane requirement.
options.text: Finish the turn in whichever lane looks most open

options.rationale: Wrong: straddling markings violates the stay-inside-marked-lanes rule.
options.text: Straddle the lane line through the turn for extra room

items.stem: Practice question: which description follows the taught rule for lane use through turns and intersections?

items.correct_rationale: Option A is correct: the taught practice rule starts in park or with the clutch engaged and brake held, then checks lamps and gauges before moving.

options.rationale: Starting secured with brake held and checking lamps and gauges matches the taught steps.
options.text: Begin in park or clutch engaged with brake held, then check lamps and gauges

options.rationale: Wrong: moving before selecting a gear and checking controls skips required startup steps.
options.text: Roll forward first then select a gear and glance at gauges later

options.rationale: Wrong: releasing the brake before securing the selector risks unintended motion.
options.text: Release the brake first then check lamps after driving away

options.rationale: Wrong: skipping lamp and gauge checks omits the taught pre-move verification.
options.text: Skip all checks and accelerate as soon as the engine starts

items.stem: Practice question: which startup sequence matches the taught practice steps before moving the car?

items.correct_rationale: Option D is correct: the taught practice rule calls for looking through the rear window with an arm over the passenger seat, steering toward the intended rear path, and never backing on a freeway or interstate.

options.rationale: Wrong: mirrors alone miss the area directly behind the vehicle.
options.text: Rely only on mirrors and steer without looking back

options.rationale: Wrong: backing on a freeway or interstate is barred in the taught rule.
options.text: Back up on the freeway shoulder when you miss an exit

options.rationale: Wrong: steering opposite the intended rear path sends the rear the wrong way.
options.text: Look forward and steer opposite the intended rear path

options.rationale: Looking through the rear window and steering toward the rear path reflects the taught rule.
options.text: Look through the rear window with an arm over the seat and steer toward the rear path

items.stem: Practice question: which backing method matches the taught practice rule?

items.correct_rationale: Option B is correct: the merging practice rule requires yielding to traffic already in the continuing lane and never driving across or inside the solid-white gore area.

options.rationale: Wrong: cutting across the gore area violates the taught prohibition.
options.text: Drive across the solid-white gore area to merge sooner

options.rationale: Yielding to continuing traffic and avoiding the gore area matches the taught rule.
options.text: Yield to traffic in the continuing lane and stay out of the gore area

options.rationale: Wrong: continuing traffic holds priority, so forcing entry is incorrect.
options.text: Force entry because merging traffic has priority

options.rationale: Wrong: stopping inside the gore zone still enters the barred area.
options.text: Stop inside the gore area to wait for a gap

items.stem: Practice question: you enter a freeway from an on-ramp. Which action matches the taught merging practice?

items.correct_rationale: Option C is correct: the congested-merge practice uses the zipper method by filling both lanes to the merge point and then alternating entry into the single lane.

options.rationale: Wrong: leaving one lane empty early wastes capacity and is not the zipper method.
options.text: Leave one lane empty far back and merge very early

options.rationale: Wrong: racing to the front and shoving in is not alternating entry.
options.text: Race to the front and push in ahead of everyone

options.rationale: Filling both lanes to the point and alternating matches the taught zipper method.
options.text: Use both lanes to the merge point then take turns entering one by one

options.rationale: Wrong: stopping both lanes blocks flow rather than alternating.
options.text: Stop both lanes well before the merge point

items.stem: Practice question: two lanes narrow to one in a congested work zone. Which behavior matches the taught practice?

items.correct_rationale: Option A is correct: the passing practice requires returning no less than two hundred feet from oncoming traffic and never leaving the roadway to pass on the right.

options.rationale: Keeping ample clearance and staying on the roadway matches the taught passing rule.
options.text: Return only when well clear of oncoming traffic and stay on the roadway

options.rationale: Wrong: the shoulder is not a passing lane and leaving the roadway is barred.
options.text: Use the shoulder to pass on the right

options.rationale: Wrong: cutting back closely in front of oncoming traffic breaks the clearance rule.
options.text: Squeeze back right just ahead of oncoming traffic

options.rationale: Wrong: lingering beside the passed vehicle prolongs exposure and is unsafe.
options.text: Stay beside the passed vehicle for a long stretch

items.stem: Practice question: which return-after-passing choice matches the taught practice rule?

items.correct_rationale: Option D is correct: the taught never-pass list includes blocked views on curves or hills, intersections and stopped crosswalks, rail crossings and bridges, no-passing zones, and snowplow blade or echelon cases.
distractor_source: synthesized near-miss: straight-clear-view pass allowed confusion

options.rationale: Wrong: this describes only one barred case and omits the rest of the taught list.
options.text: Passing is barred only beside snowplows and nowhere else

options.rationale: Wrong: a blocked view on a curve or hill bars passing rather than allowing it.
options.text: Pass on a blind curve when no car is seen at the moment

options.rationale: Wrong: intersections and stopped crosswalks are on the taught never-pass list.
options.text: Pass at an intersection when the lead car pauses briefly

options.rationale: The combined list of blocked views, intersections, crossings, zones, and plows matches the taught rule.
options.text: Hold back on blind curves and hills, at intersections and crosswalks, before rails and bridges, and near plow blades

items.stem: Practice question: which choice best reflects the taught places where passing stays prohibited?

items.correct_rationale: Option A is correct: downhill parking turns the front wheels toward the curb so a tire contacts it, then sets park and the parking brake.

options.rationale: Turning toward the curb with contact then securing the car matches the downhill practice.
options.text: Turn front wheels toward the curb with tire contact, then set park and brake

options.rationale: Wrong: away from the curb is the uphill-with-curb direction, not downhill.
options.text: Turn front wheels away from the curb with no tire contact

options.rationale: Wrong: leaving the car in gear without park and brake skips the securing steps.
options.text: Leave the selector in gear with no parking brake

options.rationale: Wrong: straight wheels let a downhill car roll and omit curb blocking.
options.text: Keep wheels straight and ignore the curb

items.stem: Practice question: you park facing downhill beside a curb. Which wheel and securing steps match the taught practice?

items.correct_rationale: Option B is correct: uphill parking with a curb turns wheels away from the curb with contact, and without a curb turns them to the right, then sets park and brake.

options.rationale: Wrong: toward the curb is the downhill direction, not uphill with a curb.
options.text: Turn wheels toward the curb in every uphill case

options.rationale: Away with a curb and to the right without a curb matches the uphill practice.
options.text: Turn wheels away from a curb, or to the right where no curb exists

options.rationale: Wrong: straight wheels do not block rolling in either uphill case.
options.text: Keep wheels straight regardless of curb presence

options.rationale: Wrong: the taught rule names a direction for each uphill case.
options.text: Wheel direction does not matter when the brake is set

items.stem: Practice question: you park facing uphill. Which wheel direction matches the taught practice for curb and no-curb spots?

items.correct_rationale: Option C is correct: a controlled rail crossing requires stopping more than fifteen feet but not more than fifty feet from the nearest rail and waiting for a raised gate.

options.rationale: Wrong: stopping on or hugging the rails puts the car in the danger zone.
options.text: Stop right on the rails to look both ways

options.rationale: Wrong: driving around a lowered gate disobeys the taught wait requirement.
options.text: Drive around the lowered gate when no train is seen

options.rationale: The stopping window plus waiting for the gate matches the taught rail practice.
options.text: Stop back from the nearest rail within the taught window and wait for the gate to rise

options.rationale: Wrong: stopping far back beyond the window and then creeping onto the tracks breaks the rule.
options.text: Stop far away then creep onto the tracks to see better

items.stem: Practice question: you reach a rail crossing with flashing signals and a gate. Which stop matches the taught practice?

items.correct_rationale: Option A is correct: both directions stop on a two-lane road and on a four-lane road without a median, while only lanes behind the bus stop on a median-divided highway and on a highway with a shared center turn lane.

options.rationale: The roadway-type split between undivided and divided roads matches the taught bus practice.
options.text: Stop both ways on undivided roads but only behind the bus on divided and center-lane highways

options.rationale: Wrong: oncoming traffic on a two-lane road must also stop in the taught rule.
options.text: Only same-direction traffic ever stops for red bus lamps

options.rationale: Wrong: oncoming traffic on a median-divided highway is not required to stop in the taught rule.
options.text: Oncoming traffic must also stop on a median-divided highway

options.rationale: Wrong: proceeding past flashing red bus lamps breaks the taught stop rule.
options.text: Pass slowly past the bus when its red lamps flash

items.stem: Practice question: a school bus shows flashing red lamps. Which stopping choice matches the taught practice by roadway type?
